referenceSize.note: Aquarium-trade Cerithium species carry adult shells of about 20-30 mm (SeaLifeBase records 3.4 cm maximum for C. litteratum; CIESM describes Cerithium shells as roughly three times as long as wide with 9-11 whorls). The size gate measures the whole crawling mesh along x, from the trailing shell apex to the extended tentacle tips, so 25 mm is the crawling length; the modelled shell itself is about 21 mm along its coiling axis (see notes.shellLengthMeters in the contract).

morphology.notes: Slender turreted spire of 11 whorls with a 25 degree spire angle; four granulose spiral cords per whorl plus two marginal threads, beads aligned into weak axial ribs; body whorl slightly inflated; small oval constricted aperture with a thickened outer lip and short anterior canal notch; shell dragged behind with the coiling axis nearly horizontal, apex trailing low on the substrate and yawed to the animal's right. Small flat-soled foot, short broad snout, long slim cephalic tentacles with eyes on bulges at their outer bases, short inhalant siphon at the anterior canal.

visualDebt: Spiral cords and beads are geometric only on the last five whorls; earlier whorls carry the sculpture in the normal map alone.

Whorls are a single swept tube that overlaps itself to form sutures, with a thin columella plug closing the axis; the shell wall has no modelled thickness and the aperture interior is a shallow recessed cap behind the neck.
The operculum is not modelled and the aperture is nearly circular rather than the slightly oblique oval of real Cerithium.
The rounded shell base reads dark in the front orthographic view; base flecking and lighting could be improved.
Soft-part proportions (foot, snout, siphon) are inferred from general cerithiid anatomy rather than calibrated live photographs, and the tentacles are straight tapered tubes without curl.
